subject_session: sub-A3707 ses-200317 (walk-through); all 31 sessions for population

headline_stat.name: median held-out decoding error across sessions

stated_limitation: Head direction is measured from head-mounted LEDs, so it is the direction of the headstage, not of the gaze; small tracking errors broaden tuning curves and set a floor on the decoding error.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000939 is the Peyrache-lab mouse postsubiculum HD-cell dataset, the canonical region, species, and open-field paradigm for this phenomenon.
justification.handling: Real NWB files streamed via remfile with disk cache, correct epoch/behavioral-series alignment, NaN removal, occupancy normalization, and author labels used only for validation.
justification.analysis: Correct circular statistics with a circular-shift null (min-shift exclusion), split-half stability, held-out Bayesian decoding with a time-shuffle control, and a GLM competing direction against spike history.
justification.correctness: Every headline number reproduces exactly from the committed CSVs, values are internally consistent with the figures, and statistics rest on 2691 units across 31 sessions with proper held-out evaluation.
justification.figures: Seven figures cleanly show the effect with labeled units and sample sizes, and example cells are chosen to represent the effect being demonstrated.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate, the high 74% figure is explicitly explained, and specific real limitations (LED vs gaze, threshold dependence, uncontrolled angular velocity, opto sessions) are named.
